Interesting results:

Then inside scripts, files "scripts/foo.py" would match `!/scripts/*` → unignored, but dir pruned. Git behaves the same way actually! Let me verify with real git... git not necessarily available? Probably is. But git semantics: "It is not possible to re-include a file if a parent directory of that file is excluded." So git would also show nothing. So matching git, this case can't work.

Hmm wait, but `!/scripts/**` now works because `**` regex probably matches "scripts/" itself (zero or more). pathspec: `scripts/**` → `^scripts(?:/|(?=/))..*$`? Apparently it matched "scripts/".

So the remaining `!/scripts/*` case behaves like git — parent dir excluded → contents can't be re-included. That's arguably correct. But the user listed it as a failing trial they expected to work... The user's expectation might be wrong for that one; dvc follows git semantics.
